cards.title: Source rights and full-budget feasibility
cards.question: Which source-rights resolution route should anchor the v1 capability and cost matrix?

owner_answer.label: Keep Yahoo/Grow; verify uses and investigate gaps (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision 1, call_a9fb61df13c0420cb65c12f1b5972650
owner_answer.meaning: Preferred candidate direction selected. Per-listing coverage and storage/training/derived-display/Anthropic-sharing rights and full-budget evidence remain unresolved. Research alternatives for documented gaps only. No paid upgrade or activation authorised.

dev_refinement.direction: Consider Twelve Data Basic/Free for dev, alongside synthetic fixtures.
dev_refinement.constraint: Weighted credits, not necessarily800HTTPrequests. Actual account, listing/endpoint entitlements and storage/training/LLM rights still require verification. No provider calls or setup authorised.

options.label: Keep Yahoo/Grow candidates with explicit per-use gates (Recommended)
options.approach: Retain the requested source mixture as candidates. Obtain written clarification of storage, derived features, historical training/non-display, LLM transmission and display rights for each use/listing. Plan source adapters and daily/unavailable states now; activate no unsupported use.
options.impact_tradeoff: Preserves the preferred providers and the £100 ceiling, but some forecasting capabilities may remain gated if Grow cannot supply the required rights within budget.

options.label: Compare licensed alternatives before fixing the source plan
options.approach: Research alternative licences/quotes for the missing named uses alongside Yahoo/Grow, without subscribing. Present any change in source or promised scope for owner approval within the same £100 ceiling.
options.impact_tradeoff: Adds procurement/research effort but may resolve training rights and cross-market coverage sooner; no new paid source or larger budget is approved by the choice.

before_ux: Choose the rights-resolution route and document target versus eligible capabilities for US/UK/India; keep every agreed horizon and import method represented.
before_build: Approve adapter contracts, minimum data/history semantics, point-in-time provenance, conservative recurring costs and unsupported-state acceptance cases.
before_activation: Verify actual account/tier/exchange rights and applicable licences for each enabled use; recost subscriptions, FX/tax, Claude, AWS, evals and reserve. If infeasible, return to the owner rather than silently cutting scope.

cards.title: Ledger, imports and write ownership
cards.question: Which persistence boundary should the detailed ledger/import specification adopt?

owner_answer.label: DynamoDB + S3, with one controlled write service (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision 2, call_b4bd470284f749658ca3e84b5db62806
owner_answer.meaning: DynamoDB operational records and encrypted S3 originals selected as the storage direction. One backend write service owns owner-confirmed financial changes and corresponding audit/outbox evidence; agents may prepare drafts but cannot commit directly. Access patterns, precision, concurrency, large imports, query fit, recovery and export decisions remain open. No build or full architecture approval.

options.label: DynamoDB with staged immutable imports (Recommended)
options.approach: Keep the preferred DynamoDB operational core and encrypted S3 originals. One application write service owns ledger changes, audit/outbox and owner-approved commit visibility; agents may create typed drafts but never commit financial records directly. Define access patterns and large-import staging before keys.
options.impact_tradeoff: Fits the requested serverless stack, but all readers/projections must honour the same commit marker and investigation queries need explicit indexes.

options.label: Relational ledger with AWS serverless services around it
options.approach: Keep S3, Lambda and the same draft/approval/write-service ownership, but compare a managed relational ledger for financial transactions and query-intensive audit. Select it only after its AWS cost and connectivity fit are accepted.
options.impact_tradeoff: Simplifies some multi-row/query invariants but adds connection, network and recurring-cost concerns. This explicitly changes the preferred storage direction and may fail the budget fit.

before_ux: Choose the persistence direction and approve the domain/write boundary under existing MP-12.
Decide owner export formats and optional file interchange separately from MA retirement; no live coupling or cutover is implied.
before_build: Specify financial precision, XIRR/root/FX/cash-flow conventions, duplicate identity, concurrent corrections, atomic audit/outbox and import visibility including beyond DynamoDB transaction limits.
before_activation: Run approved crash/replay/restore proofs and reconcile staged or orphaned objects before real ledger data is accepted.

cards.title: Durable workflow orchestration
cards.question: Where should long-lived import, training, approval and recovery workflow state be defined?

owner_answer.label: Lambda Durable Functions with Python workflows
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision3, call_05c334b9e81044c49fe0bd4c36005dfe
owner_answer.meaning: Use Lambda Durable Functions with Python as primary orchestration; supersedes the maker Step Functions Standard recommendation. Retain SQS buffering, EventBridge Scheduler clocks and DynamoDB business/approval records. Runtime/OCI/SDK/region/cost, deterministic replay, external effects, cancellation and recovery require proof. No default Step Functions deployment, build or full baseline approval.

reaffirmation.source: Owner reply to FastAPI/hybrid clarification, call_a47cfcc9de014354bee16cbbd06e44c2
reaffirmation.scope: Ordinary Lambda hosts FastAPI. Durable Functions owns background workflows. No Step Functions in the initial architecture; reconsider only for a justified workflow with a separate owner decision.

options.label: Step Functions Standard (Recommended)
options.approach: Use a small set of explicit cross-service state machines for import and train/evaluate/approve flows; SQS buffers work and Scheduler provides clocks. Store opaque evidence references in workflow state.
options.impact_tradeoff: Matches visual/admin investigation and native SageMaker joins; state-transition/history charges and state-machine contracts need costing.

options.label: Lambda Durable Functions
options.approach: Use checkpointed Python workflow code with durable steps/waits and typed continuation references. Keep queue, idempotency and external ambiguity contracts equivalent.
options.impact_tradeoff: Keeps orchestration beside business logic, but runtime/container/SDK/region fit, replay discipline and inspection experience need explicit evidence.

before_ux: Select one primary orchestrator and agree accepted/pending/approved/executing/failed/reconcile-required/cancelled state meanings.
before_build: Approve retries, leases, ordering, scheduler-versus-worker DLQs, side-effect ambiguity, stale approvals, cancellation and retention. Verify packaging support rather than equating managed-runtime listings with all container support.
before_activation: Exercise duplicate delivery, crash boundaries, expired approvals and denied cross-environment replay; no exactly-once external-call claim.

cards.title: ML training and serving execution
cards.question: Which bounded AWS execution approach should carry the same scientific protocol?

owner_answer.label: Selective SageMaker training + portable Lambda inference (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision4, call_5db1e80f68f9402884ff4dfbbd42a2bf
owner_answer.meaning: Use capped on-demand CPU SageMaker candidate training/evaluation, approved portable artefacts in S3, Lambda inference where compatible and stored daily forecast results; no always-on inference endpoint by default. Python Lambda Durable Functions coordinates jobs and approvals; Claude remains on Anthropic. Resource/dependency/region/cost, exact model/task catalogue, job/replay/cancellation and scientific promotion proof remain open. No training, paid call, provisioning or whole-baseline approval.

options.label: Selective SageMaker training, portable serving (Recommended)
options.approach: Use capped on-demand CPU SageMaker candidate training/evaluation where its managed evidence is useful; export approved artefacts for Lambda inference and store daily forecast results. Keep no always-on endpoint by default.
options.impact_tradeoff: Follows the requested SageMaker direction while limiting idle cost; container/job setup and artifact compatibility still need proof.

options.label: Bounded portable AWS training jobs
options.approach: Use reproducible Lambda jobs while within resource limits and a bounded AWS container job when they are exceeded; keep artefact registry/evidence in the same contracts. Revisit SageMaker only when its operational benefit is demonstrated.
options.impact_tradeoff: Can reduce service surface for a small dataset, but the project must own more job lifecycle and experiment-evidence plumbing.

before_ux: Choose the execution direction and separate training, calibration, inference and serving responsibilities.
before_build: Approve job caps/cadence, artifact format, model/data/version record, resource envelopes and workflow cancellation/recovery; keep exact model counts evidence-based.
before_activation: Benchmark representative approved workloads and full cost. If Serverless Inference is considered, explicitly handle its VPC/network-isolation/data-capture/Model-Monitor exclusions.

cards.decision_semantics: Selecting an option authorises recording a proposed architecture direction only. It does not run paid proofs, implement/deploy, promote a model, alter data, or settle unlisted numerical policy details.

cards.title: Forecast experiments, probability calibration and recommendations
cards.question: How broadly should the first scientific qualification programme search for an edge?

owner_answer.label: Baselines first, then bounded challengers (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision5, call_ff13748f07f04b93ac2f8611c0f62c9c
owner_answer.meaning: Establish transparent rules/statistical/simple numerical baselines, then qualify a bounded set of stronger challengers. Add news, pattern, analog/event and LLM-derived factors only with incremental-value evidence. Preserve all agreed horizons and F1–F8 capabilities. Exact tasks, folds, catalogue, search caps, calibration/eligibility/abstention and rollback policies remain open. Shadow evidence and owner approval precede promotion. No training or complete baseline/build approval.

options.label: Baselines first, bounded challengers (Recommended)
options.approach: Freeze task/horizon/known-at/outcome contracts first. Establish rules, historical/risk and simple linear/logistic baselines, then qualify a bounded gradient-boosted/quantile challenger and individually justified news/pattern/analog factors.
options.impact_tradeoff: Gives clearer incremental-value and leakage evidence within the budget; advanced modules may stay in shadow or unavailable longer while outcomes mature.

options.label: Qualify the wider feature/model set together
options.approach: Evaluate regime, risk, analog/event, boosted/quantile and bounded LLM-derived/pattern feature candidates in the initial programme using a predeclared search budget and identical strict temporal validation.
options.impact_tradeoff: May discover useful interactions earlier, but increases data needs, selection bias controls, experiment cost and the explanation burden.

before_ux: Choose experiment breadth; approve target/interval/risk meanings and the distinction between rule strength, calibrated probability, preference ranking and scenario. Keep agreed horizons and confirmed 35/40/25 ranking weights unchanged.
before_build: Approve horizon-specific folds/purge, data vintages, benchmark/cash-flow/FX conventions, calibration/proper losses, ablations, multiple-testing/search limits, sparse evidence and action eligibility. No new threshold is implied by either option.
before_activation: Use mature independent outcomes and prospective shadow where historical contamination cannot be bounded; present evidence for owner model promotion. Define any safety-disable/rollback authority separately.

cards.decision_semantics: Selecting an option authorises recording a proposed architecture direction only. It does not run paid proofs, implement/deploy, promote a model, alter data, or settle unlisted numerical policy details.

cards.title: Anthropic route, memory, cache and batch boundaries
cards.question: How should Claude responsibilities be packaged while retaining the agreed direct SDK loop?

owner_answer.label: Separate Lambda workers for each task route
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision6, call_10ac80fb76ea407d81b99e3ae9e092f4
owner_answer.meaning: Deploy each evaluated Claude task route as a separate Lambda worker with distinct permissions and route-specific queue/context/tool/budget/eval controls, sharing the versioned typed Anthropic client-runner library. Claude stays hosted on Anthropic. Tool-free untrusted extraction, public/private research separation, scoped memory, measured cache and deadline-aware nonurgent batches remain required. Exact route/worker/model catalogue, limits, IAM, memory/retention and cost require specification; no direct ledger commits, promotion, paid calls or build approval.

options.label: Shared bounded runner with scoped task routes (Recommended)
options.approach: Use one typed Anthropic client-runner library with a small evaluated task-route catalogue and per-route context/tool/cost/eval policy. Keep deterministic analyst/grader/budget/ops responsibilities explicit; use Haiku/Sonnet classes only where justified.
options.impact_tradeoff: Reduces duplicated loop/policy code, but route isolation, tool narrowing and memory scope must be tested carefully.

options.label: Separate task workers using the same runner library
options.approach: Package research/extraction/explanation routes into independent Lambda workers with distinct IAM and queues, while reusing the same SDK/policy/evidence library and model-class evaluation.
options.impact_tradeoff: Provides stronger deployment/permission separation, but adds queue, configuration, monitoring and release joins for a personal app.

before_ux: Approve the role/route catalogue and public/private outbound-context boundary; nine logical responsibilities do not become nine LLMs by default.
before_build: Pin evaluated models/prompts/tools/effort, claim-grounding and fail-closed policy. Specify sourced/tainted/revisable memory, cache eligibility/economics and deadline-aware batch item reconciliation.
before_activation: Verify permitted provider handling and actual credit. Immediate alerts and fresh 07:30 briefing delivery must not depend on a newly submitted batch; no automatic paid fallback or cache warming.

cards.title: Identity, session recovery and action-bound step-up
cards.question: Which server-verifiable fresh-authentication path should protect sensitive owner actions?

owner_answer.label: Cognito assurance and freshness checks (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision7, call_cedccedd1b25426fa82d632a0224da7e
owner_answer.meaning: Use backend-verified Cognito authentication strength/freshness for sensitive actions and prompt when proof is insufficient. Use verified fresh sign-in when assurance feature is unavailable, meeting the same action policy or deny. Retain Apple/Google/passkeys, verified linking and recovery requirements. Bind approval to exact owner/environment/action/payload/version/expiry and recheck at execution. Tier/rollout/provider/cost and precise policy/session/recovery proofs remain open; no setup, upgrade or build approval.

options.label: Cognito assurance-based step-up where supported (Recommended)
options.approach: Design sensitive actions around Cognito server-verified authentication freshness/assurance claims and an action-bound challenge, subject to current plan/region/rollout support. Use an explicitly verified fresh-sign-in path when that assurance capability is unavailable.
options.impact_tradeoff: Can give a clearer assurance contract, but actual feature availability and Apple/Google/passkey behaviour must be validated before the UX promises it.

options.label: Fresh managed sign-in for each protected action class
options.approach: Start with an explicit Cognito managed-login reauthentication sequence, verified server-side and bound to the exact action/environment/payload/expiry; add richer assurance-level policy later.
options.impact_tradeoff: Simpler initial feature dependency, but may require more sign-in interactions and still needs proof of freshness rather than token refresh alone.

before_ux: Choose the protected-action mechanism under MP-11 and approve sensitive-action classes, verified account linking and recovery journeys. Apple, Google, passkeys and the agreed recovery redundancy remain required in both options.
before_build: Define cookie/CSRF versus native PKCE/secure-storage boundaries, account linking by verified control, session/device revocation and approval payload/version binding. Local biometric unlock alone grants no server authority.
before_activation: Verify actual Cognito feature compatibility and exercise lost-device, final-method unlink, stale approval, revoked session and cross-environment token cases.

cards.decision_semantics: Selecting an option authorises recording a proposed architecture direction only. It does not run paid proofs, implement/deploy, promote a model, alter data, or settle unlisted numerical policy details.

cards.title: Admin scope, audit integrity, retention and recovery
cards.question: How much administration depth should be specified for the first UX baseline?

owner_answer.label: Full admin journeys before first build (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision8, call_aff832db6269412aabc56a31308ef12c
owner_answer.meaning: Specify all identified admin domains/policies/contracts now; after architecture agreement, design complete admin investigation, comparison, configuration, approval, failure and recovery journeys within the full UX baseline before first application build. Implementation remains phased. Preserve confirmed retention/deletion and main-app cost visibility; exact policies/RPO/RTO/integrity/recovery proofs remain open. No UX execution, deletion, restore, paid call or build approval.

options.label: Full investigation and administration UX before first build (Recommended)
options.approach: Design all identified admin investigation, comparison, recovery and configuration workflows as part of the initial complete UX baseline, then phase their implementation.
options.impact_tradeoff: Provides more end-to-end interaction detail up front, but lengthens UX preparation and requires resolving more policies before product work can start.

options.label: All admin domains with a defined launch minimum
options.approach: Specify Files/Imports, Audit, Runs/Health, Agents/Models/Evals, Approvals/Config, Costs/Budgets, Incidents/Recovery and Identity/Devices now. Within each, identify required launch controls and later investigation depth; preserve full traceability from the first useful layer.
options.impact_tradeoff: Makes the whole structure explicit before UX while keeping the initial screen/action set bounded. Detailed later controls remain tracked rather than silently dropped.

before_ux: Approve domain/navigation/action boundaries, the privileged threat model and minimal protected evidence. Keep confirmed 24-month renewable original archive, owner deletion, telemetry retention and monthly/change-triggered exercises unchanged.
before_build: Resolve record-class retention/deletion, S3 versions/derivatives/provider copies/training data/labels/backups, restore tombstones, audit integrity claims, RPO/RTO, replay authority and separate financial-versus-operational alert classes.
before_activation: Demonstrate isolated restore, reapplication of deletions, lineage integrity and denied recovery actions; verify push permission/channel behaviour and approved critical quiet-hour exceptions.

cards.decision_semantics: Selecting an option authorises recording a proposed architecture direction only. It does not run paid proofs, implement/deploy, promote a model, alter data, or settle unlisted numerical policy details.

cards.title: Guardrails and evaluation harness
cards.question: Which harness should organise the same required safety, regression and capability evidence?

owner_answer.label: Inspect AI + deterministic checks (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision9, call_d74495e8a3a24affa87c5c0ac5e55ff2
owner_answer.meaning: Use Inspect AI with typed MP-specific deterministic checks for agent scenarios, transcripts, scoring/rescoring and reports. Runtime guardrails stay in application policy code; pytest stays for unit/integration/offline tests; numerical prediction validation remains separate. T0/T1/T2, online/human judging, exact cases/trials/thresholds/version/adapters/privacy/cost/CI policies remain to specify. No evaluation execution, install, model call, independent review or build approval.

options.label: Inspect AI with typed deterministic checks (Recommended)
options.approach: Use an Inspect AI evaluation harness for tagged cases, transcripts and deterministic/model scoring, integrated with offline replays and the MP manifests. Keep runtime guardrails in application policy code, independent of the evaluation harness.
options.impact_tradeoff: Reuses established evaluation structure and rescore workflows, but adds a dependency and requires careful privacy, budget and adapter contracts.

options.label: Project-owned pytest-based evaluation harness
options.approach: Use typed test/replay fixtures and custom result records in the existing Python test ecosystem; implement model-judge and replay/scoring integrations explicitly.
options.impact_tradeoff: Keeps the dependency surface smaller, but MP must maintain equivalent case taxonomy, rescoring, trial aggregation, provenance and report tooling.

before_ux: Select the harness and approve failure taxonomy, runtime policy boundaries and required unknown/refused/incomplete UI states.
before_build: Specify change-triggered offline T0, bounded affected-route live T1 and model/release qualification T2; choose trial counts, failure limits and judge eligibility from risk and budget rather than importing MA numbers. Human labels/uncertainty and incident-to-regression handling are explicit; predictive ML evaluation remains separate.
before_activation: Run live evaluations only under separately approved spend; budget exhaustion or missing evidence is incomplete, never green. Calibrated judges remain advisory until the agreed held-out evidence supports their role.

cards.title: Client rendering and shared contracts
cards.question: Which web rendering boundary should the UX specifications assume?

owner_answer.label: Static SvelteKit PWA + authenticated FastAPI (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision10, call_1634cf059af44442bc65aae7a993c72f
owner_answer.meaning: Serve the prebuilt interactive SvelteKit PWA shell/assets through CloudFront from a private S3 origin. Private financial data/commands use authenticated FastAPI on ordinary Lambda; no separate SvelteKit SSR runtime selected. Retain adaptive PWA, native Swift/SwiftUI+RN and typed API/event contracts. Startup/performance, sessions/cache/offline privacy, SSE/push/updates/device/bridge/accessibility proofs remain open. No UI build, hosting setup, deployment or complete baseline approval.

options.label: Static SvelteKit PWA plus authenticated API (Recommended)
options.approach: Use a static SvelteKit shell on private S3/CloudFront and explicit authenticated API/session contracts. Keep Swift/SwiftUI surfaces and native cache/device responsibilities within the agreed RN navigation/typed-bridge shell.
options.impact_tradeoff: Fits the low-idle-cost plan and clear backend boundary, but private page data, offline handling and session checks must be designed explicitly rather than assumed server-rendered.

options.label: SvelteKit server rendering on an AWS runtime
options.approach: Add an AWS-hosted SvelteKit server for approved server-rendered/session use cases while retaining FastAPI as the domain API and the same Swift/RN ownership.
options.impact_tradeoff: Can support server-side rendering and session flows directly, but adds a runtime, deployment/security joins and cost to justify.

before_ux: Select rendering mode and freeze typed API/event/action/error/proof contracts plus supported web/Apple device capabilities, including a precise interpretation of Duo. Both options retain SvelteKit3 and Swift/SwiftUI+RN as requested.
before_build: Define offline privacy/clearance, stale/unavailable/in-practice states, resumable SSE/auth refresh, service-worker/app updates, push and native bridge versioning. Separate shared contracts from separate web/native implementation stories.
before_activation: Verify actual browser/OS push/offline/secure-storage and accessibility behaviour on supported devices; the existing React architecture Site remains a separate documentation artifact.

cards.title: Environment isolation, region, compatibility and whole-system recost
cards.question: Which environment-isolation direction should the final deployment comparison assume?

owner_answer.label: Separate dev/prod AWS accounts (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision11, call_bfbd4f35cfa048d2ab7165339ed42c25
owner_answer.meaning: Use separate dev/prod AWS workload accounts under consolidated billing, with environment-specific identities/resources/deployment/write authority and combined MP cost visibility. Keep £100 all-in aggregate, £70 operation/£30 reserve; no multiplied free-tier/provider credits. Exact account/organisation/roles, cheapest suitable compatible region, network/runtime/IaC/cost/release/recovery evidence remain open. No account creation, billing/org change, credentials, deployment or complete baseline approval.

options.label: Separate dev/prod AWS accounts (Recommended)
options.approach: Use separate accounts and environment-scoped OIDC deployment roles, with consolidated cost visibility and the same least-complex initial networking direction.
options.impact_tradeoff: Stronger account-level isolation, with extra organisational/role/deployment administration. Organizations itself has no additional service charge; resource usage and any duplicated services still need aggregate costing. Free-tier/credit benefits must not be assumed per account.

options.label: One account with strictly separated dev/prod resources
options.approach: Compare suitable regions and start with distinct environment resources/identities/IAM/write authority in one account; customer-VPC-unattached external API Lambdas are the initial candidate. Optional private jobs get a separately justified network scope.
options.impact_tradeoff: Reduces account administration and shared-service duplication, but same-account privileged blast radius and shared quotas require explicit controls and acceptance.

before_ux: Choose the isolation direction and documented network boundaries. Keep cheapest suitable region selection evidence-based; do not inherit MA account IDs, domains, CIDRs, proxies, IaC or permissions.
before_build: Approve the exact compatible runtime/SDK/adapter/framework/architecture matrix and one IaC tool, immutable artifact promotion, vulnerability exceptions, rollback and offline/live gate selection. Reprice baseline/stress including active stream hours, reads, telemetry cardinality, trials, backups and collectors.
before_activation: Verify actual region availability, service quotas, pricing, entitlements and credit scope; obtain deployment authority separately. If any choice fails compatibility or the £70 operating envelope plus £30 reserve, reopen the affected decision before proceeding.

recommendation_history.basis: Initial maker pack prioritised one-account administration for a personal app.

Revised before asking ARC-11: separate dev/prod accounts better contain experimental agent/eval/import access to production holdings. AWS documents environment isolation and no additional Organizations service charge; actual resource costs and operational overhead remain. No owner selection yet.

cards.title: Architecture and phase-document freeze
cards.question: Which canonical documentation structure should be the approved handoff into UX?

owner_answer.label: Architecture-area specs + linked phases/stories (Recommended)
owner_answer.source: Owner reply to architecture decision12, call_85c73d42e75a44b2b629371b22c08dab
owner_answer.meaning: Use central architecture-area specs/journeys and shared decisions/contracts, linked to one page per MP phase and individual Jira stories with source, contract and acceptance-test/UX trace. Complete and present the detailed pack for separate owner sign-off before UX. This settles organisation only; detailed gap/specification/phase/story/visual/cost closure and explicit final architecture, UX, publication/review/PR/build approvals remain separate.

options.label: Architecture areas plus linked phase pages and story catalogue (Recommended)
options.approach: Follow MA's useful organisation: one architecture map; detailed domain/technical area specs and journeys; a decision/contract register; one phase page per MP layer; and individual stories linked to sources, contracts, cases and planned UX states.
options.impact_tradeoff: Keeps reusable architecture decisions in one place while making each phase complete and navigable. Links and versioned publication receipts need disciplined maintenance.

options.label: Phase-contained specifications with a shared contract register
options.approach: Make each MP phase page the main reading unit containing its relevant architecture, journey and acceptance detail; keep cross-phase contracts/ADRs central and link repeated concepts rather than copy them.
options.impact_tradeoff: Provides a phase-by-phase reading path, but cross-cutting admin/security/eval requirements need especially careful ownership and cross-phase consistency checks.

before_ux: Approve one phase/dependency map and document ownership/naming; every gap has a disposition, owner and explicit deferred activation condition. Architecture decisions are either answered or clearly block the freeze. No UX starts merely because this packet exists.
Explicitly decide optional first-party UI personalisation scope; default to stable owner-configurable ordering. No MA autonomous layout or alert-policy learning is silently imported.
before_build: Create/read back approved phasewise MP Confluence pages and actual Jira stories with acceptance criteria, source/contract/test/UX links, dependencies and readiness labels. Inspect referenced rich visuals before accepting them as UX specifications. Preserve historical docs and superseded IDs.
before_activation: After separately approved complete UX/prototype and all layer/release evidence, obtain implementation and later deployment/spend authority. Documentation, Jira Done and diagram publication alone never certify a working system.

limits: These twelve grouped decisions do not replace the detailed gap register or turn unsupplied thresholds into defaults.
Architecture selection and empirical proof are separate gates; real data rights can remain activation gates only when the pre-UX design honestly supports the resulting unavailable states.
No option is selected automatically. An owner answer changes a direction only; unresolved parameters and acceptance evidence must still be completed.
No paid research, live evaluation, cloud mutation, application implementation or publication is run by this file.
